name: Música pitiusa
lineage: Complete instrumental ball pagès practice specified in the2012 Consell d’Eivissa heritage inventory: a castanyoler and a sonador playing flaüta and tambor together, supporting the four named dances. Three sound-source roles, zero singer roles in the positive official performer inventory. The federation separately documents melodic fragment elaboration and rhythmic improvisation. This is a historical practice realization, not an assertion about every current performance; its complete2012instrument list excludes the espasí that the newer federation page identifies as a later dance-use addition from caramelles. No invented named performer or claim to a particular2025recording with placeholder credits. Authored controlled live-room recording of the complete documented instrumental practice. Broad improvOnFrame follows the source-positive oral melodic-fragment elaboration over dance metre; not jazz or an invented harmonic progression. Flaüta retains its oleander duct-flute body with three finger holes, operated one-handed beside the drum; exact tuning and metal inlay unspecified. Tambor retains a hollow pine body, two skin heads, rope tension and fibre buzzing cord; goat skin is selected from the documented goat/rabbit possibilities, not asserted universal. Large juniper castanyoles retain paired halves with separating badall and hand ties. Neutral numeric axes are editorial scaffolding. Existing Basque txistu, region-specific tabor and differently constructed concert/flamenco castanets are not silently relabeled; three isolated owners preserve regional identity without shared edits. Global temperament and capture hardware omitted.
